Token handling for the EGRADX server SDK for Node; the counterpart of the Java `egradx-web-security`.

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `createTokenVerifier({ issuer, publicKey? \| jwksUri? })` | Verifies RS256 access tokens (signature, issuer, expiry, `typ: access`, the EGRADX session claims) into an `EgradxUserTokenContext`, the same fields as Java's. The key is a PEM or key object, or comes from a JWKS URL, or is discovered from `${issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`. A refused token throws `TokenRejectedException` (401). |
| `createServiceTokenManager({ issuer \| tokenEndpoint, clientId, clientSecret })` | Client-credentials tokens for calling other services: discovered, cached until shortly before expiry, one request for concurrent callers. |

Tests sign tokens with the claims Java's `EgradxTokenIssuer` issues. A token from a running Java `egradx-auth` was also verified with this package; see docs/architecture/restructure-log.md, step 5.

## Classes

### TokenRejectedException

A presented token was refused: bad signature, wrong issuer, expired, or not an EGRADX access token.

### ServiceTokenManager

#### Methods

##### getAccessToken()

```ts
getAccessToken(): Promise<string>;
```

## Functions

### createServiceTokenManager()

```ts
function createServiceTokenManager(options): ServiceTokenManager;
```

Service-to-service tokens with the client-credentials grant: the Node counterpart of the Java SDK's
EgradxServiceTokenManager. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer …`; to act on behalf of the
calling user, forward their token instead.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`ServiceTokenOptions`](#servicetokenoptions) |
